Here’s a quick roundup of the most talked‑about crime‑thriller films that hit theaters (or streaming platforms) in 2020.  These picks blend suspense, gritty storytelling, and strong performances, and they’re the ones critics and audiences alike were raving about.

| # | Title | Director | Key Cast | Why It Stood Out |
|---|-------|----------|----------|------------------|
| 1 | **The Irishman** | Martin Scorsese | Robert De Niro, Al Pacino, Joe Pesci | Scorsese’s epic saga of organized‑crime life, with De Niro’s masterful performance and a groundbreaking de‑facing technique. |
| 2 | **The Trial of the Chicago 7** | Aaron Sorkin | Ewan McGregor, Sacha Baron Cohen, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II | A courtroom thriller that blends real‑world politics with sharp dialogue and a tense, almost documentary‑style feel. |
| 3 | **The Last Duel** | Ridley Scott | Matt Damon, Adam Driver, Jodie Comer | A gritty, historically grounded crime‑drama that turns a medieval duel into a modern thriller about truth and justice. |
| 4 | **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | A psychological crime‑thriller that reimagines the classic horror story as a tense cat‑and‑mouse chase. |
| 5 | **The Gentlemen** (2019‑2020 release window) | Guy Ritchie | Matthew McConaughey, Charlie Hunnam, Michelle Dockery | Ritchie’s signature fast‑paced crime comedy‑thriller that kept audiences on edge with its twists and witty banter. |
| 6 | **The Last of Us** (TV series, 2020) | Craig Mazin, Neil Druckmann | Pedro Pascal, Bella Ramsey | Though a TV series, it’s a crime‑thriller‑driven narrative that explores survival, betrayal, and moral gray areas in a post‑apocalyptic world. |
| 7 | **The Last of Us** (video game adaptation, 2020) | Neil Druckmann | Pedro Pascal, Bella Ramsey | The game’s cinematic storytelling and intense action sequences made it a standout crime‑thriller experience. |
| 8 | **The Last of Us** (video game adaptation, 2020) | Neil Druckmann | Pedro Pascal, Bella Ramsey | The game’s cinematic storytelling and intense action sequences made it a standout crime‑thriller experience. |

> **Note:** Some titles (like *The Last of Us*) straddle the line between video game adaptations and crime‑thriller storytelling, but they were widely discussed in 2020’s crime‑thriller conversation.

If you’re looking for a deeper dive into any of these films—plot summaries, critical reception, or behind‑the‑scenes trivia—just let me know!
